claims.claim: Tasquinimod, which shares the N-methyl quinolin-2(1H)-one core with the query, is reported to have excellent oral bioavailability and oral absorption in humans, providing scaffold-level support for F >= 20%.

Doravirine, an N-methyl azole/chlorophenyl drug with a lactam-containing heteroaromatic core, has absolute oral bioavailability of 64% from a 100 mg tablet and modeled F values of 0.82-0.895; its bioavailability is not significantly affected by food, relevant to the fed-state condition.
Chlorophenyl triazolobenzodiazepine analogs (alprazolam, triazolam, brotizolam) have absolute/relative oral bioavailability values of 44-100%, all above the 20% threshold.
Trazodone, a chlorophenyl heteroaromatic lactam with a basic amine, has absolute oral bioavailability of 65-90% in humans.

Additional oral drugs with chlorophenyl/heteroaromatic or basic-amine features (fasudil, pridopidine, CPI-0610, baclofen) report absolute F values of 69-86% or qualitative high/good oral availability; none provides affirmative evidence for F < 20%.
